title: The Normal Distribution and the Central Limit Theorem

blocks.text: Why do so many phenomena in nature and computing follow a bell-shaped curve? The answer lies in the Central Limit Theorem.

blocks.markdown: The normal distribution, often called the Gaussian distribution, is a continuous probability distribution characterized by its bell-shaped curve. It is defined by two parameters: the mean $\mu$ and the standard deviation $\sigma$. The central limit theorem (CLT) is a fundamental theorem in probability theory that explains why many distributions tend to be approximately normal under certain conditions.

blocks.title: Normal Distribution
blocks.text: The normal distribution is a probability distribution that is symmetric about the mean, showing that data near the mean are more frequent in occurrence than data far from the mean. It is defined by the probability density function: \( f(x | \mu, \sigma) = \frac{1}{\sigma \sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}} \).

blocks.caption: Probability density function of the normal distribution.

blocks.markdown: The Central Limit Theorem states that the distribution of the sum (or average) of a large number of independent, identically distributed variables approaches a normal distribution, regardless of the original distribution of the variables.

blocks.title: Central Limit Theorem
blocks.text: For a large enough sample size, the sampling distribution of the sample mean will be approximately normally distributed, regardless of the shape of the original population distribution.

blocks.title: Applying the Central Limit Theorem
blocks.prompt: Suppose we have a population with mean $\mu = 50$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 10$. If we take a sample of size $n = 30$, what is the approximate distribution of the sample mean?

steps.text: Identify the mean of the population, which is $\mu = 50$.
Identify the standard deviation of the population, which is $\sigma = 10$.
Since the sample size $n = 30$ is sufficiently large, the CLT applies.
The standard deviation of the sample mean is given by $\sigma_{\bar{x}} = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{10}{\sqrt{30}} \approx 1.83$.
Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean is approximately $N(50, 1.83^2)$.

blocks.answer: The sample mean is approximately normally distributed with mean 50 and standard deviation 1.83.

blocks.markdown: The normal distribution can also be used to approximate other distributions, such as the binomial distribution, when certain conditions are met.

blocks.title: Normal Approximation to the Binomial
blocks.text: The normal approximation to the binomial distribution is valid when the sample size $n$ is large, and both $np$ and $n(1-p)$ are greater than 5, where $p$ is the probability of success.

blocks.title: Normal Approximation of a Binomial Distribution
blocks.prompt: Consider a binomial distribution with $n = 100$ trials and probability of success $p = 0.4$. Use the normal approximation to find the probability of observing 40 or fewer successes.

steps.text: Calculate the mean of the binomial distribution: $\mu = np = 100 \times 0.4 = 40$.
Use the normal distribution $N(40, 4.9^2)$ to approximate the binomial distribution.
To find $P(X \leq 40)$, use the continuity correction: $P(X \leq 40.5)$.
Convert to the standard normal variable: $Z = \frac{40.5 - 40}{4.9} \approx 0.10$.

blocks.answer: The probability of observing 40 or fewer successes is approximately 0.54.

points: The normal distribution is characterized by its mean and standard deviation.
The Central Limit Theorem allows us to approximate the distribution of sample means as normal, given a large enough sample size.
The normal distribution can approximate the binomial distribution under certain conditions.
